Explain how a VPN works in simple words
5:26 AM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it scrambled.

Without one, your internet provider and the Wi-Fi owner can see which sites you visit. With one, your device locks (encrypts) your traffic and sends it to the VPN company's computer first. That computer unlocks it and passes it on to the website. The site sees the VPN's address, not yours.

Good for: safer public Wi-Fi, hiding your browsing from your provider, and getting around location blocks. It doesn't make you anonymous, though. The VPN company can see your traffic instead, so pick one you trust.
